> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e6b7d8c8612dc0842e0153089e99a99c4c5837a4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ec6f45b3b7f56a8efae2a6de382a59990d7aceba` — the merge of head `0b352e98aa1b9f641219c60296aea4b0b8ea3612` into base `e6b7d8c8612dc0842e0153089e99a99c4c5837a4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ec6f45b3b7f56a8efae2a6de382a59990d7aceba && git checkout ec6f45b3b7f56a8efae2a6de382a59990d7aceba
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e6b7d8c8612dc0842e0153089e99a99c4c5837a4 0b352e98aa1b9f641219c60296aea4b0b8ea3612 && git checkout -B drift-repro e6b7d8c8612dc0842e0153089e99a99c4c5837a4 && git merge --no-ff 0b352e98aa1b9f641219c60296aea4b0b8ea3612

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e6b7d8c8612dc0842e0153089e99a99c4c5837a4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e6b7d8c8612dc0842e0153089e99a99c4c5837a4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

<sub>Read: card #20249 body and its 3 comments (claim 5857174683, dev report 5858350043, amendment 5858369774); ruling record 5856869656 (#19328, batch #227 item 3, letter A — verified it is that ruling) and the retired record 5716042643 (#18058, batch #148 item 4); ruling B on #17152 (5615360777); PR #20277 object, body, 6 files, 5 commits, 35 check-runs; the full diff against merge-base a9fb83ef0; at the head: package-api.zod.ts, package-api.test.ts, packages.ts (:70–85, :675–775, :970–1075, :1098–1110, :1190–1205), packages-install-body-contract.test.ts, the D3 entry and its registry region, the changeset, strict-object.ts, suggestions.zod.ts, polarity-axes.ts, the three changeset-gate headers, pr-automation's WHICH LEVEL prose, the strictness-ledger gate and counts, the SDK install call, README and docs examples, the CLI integration/e2e bodies, hotcrm at 2f7b2326 (read-only). ### ① Derived judgments

- (a) The refusal — holds. At the spec door a wrapped body with an unknown top-level key gets ONE `unrecognized_keys` issue at path `[]` whose `keys` lists every unknown key (two at once: `bogus`, `_trace` both named in one issue), message `Unrecognized key(s) on this package install request: ` + the key(s) in backticks, an optional `Did you mean` rename, then the history sentence carrying the remedy (remove it, or spell the declared option; declared keys enumerated by `PackageInstallRequestSchema`). That is the same `strictObject` envelope the manifest's unknown keys get (probe: inner `bogus` answers `Unrecognized key(s) on this package manifest: ` at path `['manifest']`; the bare form answers the same at path `[]`). At the install door the union answers `invalid_union`, `installBodyRefusal` (packages.ts:715–747) re-parses the wrapped branch alone and surfaces its issue verbatim inside `Invalid package install body (read as the WRAPPED form …) — (body): …`, and `deps.error(…, 400)` yields `VALIDATION_ERROR` — the same `expectRefused` helper §2's manifest-inner and bare-form pins use. No alias: the `strictObject` options carry only `surface` and `history` (no `aliases`, `guidance`, `extraKeys`); no grace window: `catchall.type=never`, constructor `ZodClosedObject`, no env switch. Near-miss: the rename channel pairs the caller's own key (always drawn from `issue.keys`) with a declared key read off `.shape` (tombstones excluded), budget max(2, floor(len/3)); `enabledOnInstall` → `enableOnInstall` is at distance 1 and correct. It can never name a key the caller did not send. It can offer a distance-based guess that is a different word (`overrides` → `overwrite`, distance within budget 3) — phrased as a question, the key still refused, the target always a declared key; the opposite-pole path cannot fire on this shape (poles are start/end, min/max, none declared). The `history` sentence carries no example key, so the backticked-key and `enableOnInstall` assertions in both pin files are discriminating (ablation 2 below).
- (b) The controls — hold. `.shape` = `manifest` + FIVE options: `settings`, `enableOnInstall`, `overwrite`, `platformVersion`, `artifactRef` (the card's "four" is wrong, the dev's five is right; the fixture is read off `.shape` with a pin that reds on drift). `{ manifest }` alone and `manifest` plus all five round-trip at both doors with every value carried through (probe and the spec control pins). The SDK wire body `{ manifest, settings: undefined, enableOnInstall: undefined }` survives JSON as `{ manifest }` and parses. Nothing legitimate first-party is refused: `packages/client/src/index.ts:2633–2647` sends only `manifest` / `settings` / `enableOnInstall` / `overwrite`; `client/README.md:254,261` and `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx:337` ride that call; `packages/cli/test/package-restart-acceptance.integration.test.ts:313` and `serve-package-registry-always-on.e2e.test.ts:252–254` post `{ manifest }` alone; the runtime and spec suites at head are green in CI's Test Core; the cloud-environment `install` at `client/src/index.ts:3372` posts to a different route; hotcrm at `2f7b2326e8f52adfc9efd00b68beda5348e71a1b` has zero install-door POST callers (its two `/api/v1/packages` hits are `GET` list mentions in docs). objectui `{ manifest }`: NOT MEASURED by me.
- (c) The install door — holds. §5 asserts, in order: `expectRefused` (handled, status 400, `success: false`, `error.code` VALIDATION_ERROR, no `data`), then `registry.getPackage(id)` undefined against the real `SchemaRegistry`, then `persistedDisabled().has(id)` false against the durable state file, then the message contains backticked `enabledOnInstall` AND backticked `enableOnInstall`, then the declaration's verdict last; `_source` the same minus the suggestion; the control `enableOnInstall: false` answers 201, registry `enabled === false`, persisted disabled. "Nothing installed" is asserted, not inferred. Pins are real: ablation 1 (`}).describe(...)` → `}).strip().describe(...)`, blob c4f6b506b477 → 70f87496fc7b, matching the dev's) reddened exactly the three spec refusal pins (`the bound union refuses it: expected true to be false`, 3 failed / 81 passed) and runtime §0 plus §5's two refusals (`expected 201 to be 400`, 3 failed / 29 passed) with every control green — the right mutation, since `.strip()` re-creates the pre-PR posture exactly. Ablation 2 (helper removed, bare `z.object(...).strict()`) kept status and code green but reddened the envelope assertions (spec: `expected 'Unrecognized key: "enabledOnInstall"' to contain '`enabledOnInstall`'`, 3 failed; runtime: the door message lacks the backticked key, 2 failed), so the pins hold the named-key envelope, not only the status. The §5 conversion is sound: the old `expect(status).toBe(declared ? 201 : 400)` parity was green in both directions; the new pin is load-bearing on status + code + the key named + nothing installed, and ablation 1 shows the door assertion reddening first.
- (d) The docblock — holds. The 「⛔ Do NOT close the wrapped branch with `.strict()` … (ruling A)」 sentence, the asymmetry paragraph, and the "only ONE of them is closed" heading are gone; a grep of the head file for `Do NOT close`, `STRIP mode`, `ruling A`, `5716042643`, `asymmetr` finds nothing. The new text cites the ruling record `5856869656` and the commit `c02fa1276` (verified: PR #20218's landing, 223 lines in packages.ts), with #19328 only as the convenience link — per AGENTS.md's citation rule. Every sentence is true at the head: both branches are `strictObject` (probe: `ZodClosedObject`, catchall never); `{ manifest, enabledOnInstall: false }` is refused naming the key and offering `enableOnInstall`; no alias and no grace window; the door parses the whole body through the union (packages.ts:1016) and answers what it declares; the pins live in the two named files; the request schema's own CLOSED section points at the union.
- (e) The #20219 region — holds. The residual section's only hunk is item 2 (@@ -396,8 +422,8 @@): "silently dropped on the wrapped one" → "and, since decision batch #227 item 3, on the wrapped one too". The "five classes" lead-in, "`201` either way", items 1a/1b, 3, 4 and 5 are byte-unchanged. The edited clause is true at the head (the wrapped branch refuses by name). The trailing "`201` either way" stays false as it was before this PR — #20219's.
- (f) The D3 entry — true under ruling B on #17152 (5615360777, resting on 5559778263: one D3 entry per family, naming the measured in-repo authors and the NOT-MEASURED out-of-repo population). One entry, one family (undeclared top-level keys on the wrapped install body); it names the family in `surface`, tells the author what to change in `replacement` (respell `enabledOnInstall` → `enableOnInstall`, remove any other key), names the measured first-party reach and says out-of-repo callers are NOT MEASURED, and carries all five `SemanticMigration` fields (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`; `surface` has no backticks). The registry region is a verbatim mirror: the 50 added lines equal the entry file's comment block plus fields after removing the 4-space indent. `check:migration-registry`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide` are inside the green TypeScript Type Check job. The tracker-shaped `batch #227` in `reason` is in-family (105 `batch #N` mentions in the registry at base) and outside `check:doc-authoring`'s Rule 3 population; the `history` string a caller is shown carries no tracker id.
- (g) The export and accept-set diff — the narrowing is exactly the wrapped top level. `api-surface/api.json` and `export-origins/api.json` are identical at base and head (both list `PackageInstallRequestSchema (const)` and `PackageInstallBodySchema (const)`; they record existence, not strictness); `check:api-surface`, `check:export-origins`, `check:authorable-surface` are green. The strictness ledger's `api/` row is an untriaged site total (432, counting `z.object` and `strictObject` alike), so no ledger artefact moves. Nested: `settings` is an open record (probe: arbitrary keys accepted, unchanged); `artifactRef` is `ArtifactReferenceSchema` in `marketplace.zod.ts`, unchanged base→head (it still strips an unknown key inside `artifactRef` — pre-existing, outside this card); `manifest` is `ManifestSchema`, unchanged. The bare form is `ManifestSchema`, unchanged, and refuses `bogus` exactly as before.

### ② Semver level

Declared: `@objectstack/spec` `minor`, a **BREAKING for callers of the install door** banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line-leading, marker `registered package-install-request-unknown-keys-refused`. Against the gates' stated rules this is right. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s header: during the launch window a breaking change ships as `minor` and breaking-ness is carried by the BREAKING banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition, not by the level; its level axis stands down on a `no` declaration. AGENTS.md Post-Task 3: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and `no (narrowing)` is the well-formed spelling. `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`'s header: `registered` requires every id to resolve at HEAD and at least one to be NEW in the diff (the `18.…` entry is new), while `no-migration-prescription` is REFUSED when the body carries a migration prescription — this changeset carries a FROM → TO, so the card's "wording of #19120 / #19417" (both `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, checked) could not be copied literally; the ruling record's item 2 and the card's item 4 both say `registered`, so the dev's deviation follows the ruled disposition and borrows only the prose shape. Nothing authorable is removed or renamed, so no tombstone is owed; the refusal itself carries the prescription. `Check Changeset` is green at the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Blocking: none
Non-blocking: (1) owed by the patch round — `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` :1003–1011, the install-branch comment; PR #20277 at 5941e9aa5 leaves `packages.ts` untouched (fenced by the claim, widened by amendment 5858369774). Exactly two sentences are false at the head: "⚠️ What the union does NOT refuse, deliberately: an unknown key at the TOP LEVEL of the wrapped form." and "`PackageInstallRequestSchema` is a plain `z.object` (strip mode) and its docblock forbids closing it, so `{ manifest, bogus }` parses green with `bogus` dropped" — the union refuses it, the branch is a `strictObject`, and the docblock now records the close. The block's remaining sentences ("— and this door, reading only parsed keys, now does exactly what the declaration says." and "Refusing it here without the declaration would make the published contract admit a body the door refuses; that is the declaration's decision to make.") stay true, as do the other `packages.ts` sentences naming the schema (:77, :679–735, :1104, :1196–1200); the comment is not worse than the ruled falsity. (2) `package-api.test.ts` :1080–1097 `DOOR_201_RESIDUALS`: the title and comment "the door answers 201 to all of them anyway — so this declaration is a SUBSET of the door" have been false since c02fa1276 (the door answers 400); its assertions (the declaration refuses each body) are still true, none of its bodies is a wrapped top-level unknown key, and this PR neither touches it nor changes its truth — #20219's class, not blocking for this PR. (3) The residual section's "additionally answers `201` to five classes" lead-in and item 2's trailing "`201` either way" remain false as before — #20219's, declared by the dev. (4) Cosmetic: the edited item-2 clause cites "decision batch #227 item 3" without the record id inline; the record id `5856869656` is cited 30 lines above in the same docblock. (5) Observation outside the card: `ArtifactReferenceSchema` (`marketplace.zod.ts`, unchanged here) still strips an unknown key inside `artifactRef` — pre-existing, no carrier named here. (6) The Acceptance notes are accurate: the fenced comment, the stale pin text, four→five options, the disposition deviation, the SDK re-read, objectui taken from the ruling record and not re-measured, hotcrm zero callers, out-of-repo NOT MEASURED. Closing keywords: the body closes exactly `Fixes #20249`; #19328 does not appear in the body; #20219 appears five times as prose only, never under a closing keyword.

Head-sha: `0b352e98aa1b9f641219c60296aea4b0b8ea3612`

<sub>Delta from 5941e9aa5 (PASS 5858576330): exactly one commit, `0b352e98a` (parent 5941e9aa5, no merge of main), touching `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` (+11/−8) and `packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts` (+2/−1), every changed line a `//` or ` *` comment line; the PR body was edited by the seat at 19:33:54Z. ### ① Derived judgments

- (a) The rewritten `packages.ts` paragraph (:1003–1013 at the head) — every sentence true. Sentence 1, «The TOP LEVEL of the wrapped form is closed too — by the declaration, not by this door»: `PackageInstallRequestSchema` is `strictObject({...})` at `package-api.zod.ts:228`, and the door carries no line of its own for a top-level key. Sentence 2: the ruling citation is exact (comment 5856869656 on #19328 opens «Ruling: batch #227 item 3 · letter A»); `{ manifest, enabledOnInstall: false }` fails the union — `PackageInstallBodySchema.safeParse(body)` at :1019 (the wrapped branch's `unrecognized_keys` names the key, the bare branch refuses `manifest` and lacks `id`); the verdict at :1155–1160 returns `deps.error(installBodyRefusal(...), 400)` BEFORE `installPackage` (:1193–1198), so nothing is installed; `deps.error(msg, 400)` → `apiErrorResponse` (`http-dispatcher.ts:1057–1062`) → `code: input.code ?? promoted ?? standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(400)` (`error-envelope.ts:120`) → `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[400] = 'VALIDATION_ERROR'` (`errors.zod.ts:184`); `installBodyRefusal` (:717) re-parses the wrapped branch alone and surfaces the strict close's own sentence, so the key is named — pinned by the CI-green §5 rows; «reading only parsed keys» holds: `request` (:1164), `overwrite` (:1171), `settings` (:1189) read the parsed value. Sentence 3, the restated rule «⛔ Never refuse or admit a key here that the declaration decides the other way», is true and uncontradicted in the file: the id and version legs parse the declaration's own shapes by reference (:1093, :1139); the `!pkgId` gate (:1023) refuses `''`, which `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` refuses too (:1079 says so); the 409 (:1173) is server state, not a key; `?overwrite=true` is a query parameter; the nested-shape note at :1186 says the door does NOT answer for what the declaration leaves open — the same rule from the other side. Retired reasoning gone: a grep of the head file for `strip mode`, `forbids closing`, `plain z.object`, `does NOT refuse`, `parses green`, `bogus`, `ruling A`, `5716042643` finds nothing (the base file had :1003 and :1005); the only `strip` hits are the pre-existing nested-manifest note (:1186) and the unrelated `[#15591]` read-time decoration strip (:2276–2297). Citation: the paragraph cites the ruling record `5856869656` and no tracker number at all (batch #227 is a decision-batch id). Rest of the block re-read (:970–1018): the `[#19328]` opener, the «Until this line…» history (its unknown-key row names the manifest and the bare body only), the 基本裁决原则 paragraph, the «a caller that needs an option sends the wrapped form» quotation (still at `package-api.zod.ts:443`) and «The verdict is answered after the `id` and `version` legs below» (:1093, :1139, :1155) are all true at the head.
